questions.question:
Select the correct passive form of the given sentence.

The manager lost the letter.

options.text: The letter was loss by the manager.
The letter was loose by the manager.
The letter was lost by the manager.
The letter was lose by the manager.

questions.solution:
The correct answer is** 'Option 3'.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• The **correct passive form** of the given sentence is:* The letter was lost by the manager.*
 
• The **structure of a passive sentence **is: subject + auxiliary verb (be) + past participle + (by + agent).
 
• In this case, "The letter" is the subject, "was" is the auxiliary verb (the past tense of 'be'), "lost" is the past participle of "lose", and "by the manager" is the agent.

Therefore, the **correct answer** is: *'The letter was lost by the manager.'*

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__****Option 1, **"The letter was loss by the manager," is incorrect because "loss" is a noun, not a verb.

**Option 2, **"The letter was loose by the manager," is incorrect because "loose" is an adjective, not the past participle of a verb.

**Option 4,** "The letter was lose by the manager," is incorrect because "lose" is the base form of the verb, not the past participle.

questions.question:
Choose the option that is the correct indirect form of the sentence.

Rahul asked me, "Are we going to New York next year?"

options.text: Rahul asked that are we going to New York next year.
Rahul asked me that were we going to New York next year.
Rahul asked me that would we go to New York next year?
Rahul asked me if we were going to New York next year.

questions.solution:
The correct answer is** 'Rahul asked me if we were going to New York next year.​'**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

 
• **When converting** a direct question into indirect speech, you generally use a conjunction like **"if"** or** "whether"** to connect the main clause with the question clause.
 
• **The tense **of the verb in the question clause often moves back in time (backshifts).
 
• In this case, the present tense **"are"** backshifts to **"were".**
 
• So, "Are we going to New York next year?" becomes "if we were going to New York next year."

Therefore, the **correct answer** is: *'Rahul asked me if we were going to New York next year.'*
